chunks.text: 69-year-old male, Retired, resident of Jurong West, Singapore.
Discontinued simvastatin due to muscle pain in 2015
Previous spinal anesthesia for cataract surgery in 2015, uneventful

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I’m Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who’ll be taking care of you during your surgery today. Can I briefly go over some questions to make sure everything’s in order?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. Thank you for seeing me.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: First, can you tell me a bit about why you’re having this TURP surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure. My prostate’s been enlarged for a while, and I’ve had trouble urinating—weak stream, frequent trips to the toilet at night. The urologist said it’s time to fix it before it gets worse.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Let’s go through your medications. Can you list what you’re currently taking?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Amlodipine 10mg once daily for blood pressure, lisinopril 10mg daily too. Metformin 500mg twice daily for diabetes, atorvastatin 20mg at night, omeprazole 20mg in the morning. Oh, and I stopped the aspirin 75mg as instructed a week ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Any allergies we should know about? The records say ‘no known allergies,’ but sometimes things get missed.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Hmm… I don’t think so. Wait, actually, years ago I had a rash when I took penicillin. Does that count?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Yes, that definitely counts! Can you describe the reaction? Was it a rash, swelling, or something else?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Just a red rash all over, like hives. It went away after stopping the medicine. No breathing problems or anything scary.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. I’ll update your records to note the penicillin allergy. It’s important we avoid that class of antibiotics.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. My wife made sure I fasted properly. Just sipped some water with my morning meds, but that was hours ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Any previous anesthesia experiences we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: None, this is my first time. I’ve always been healthy until this prostate issue came up.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Lastly, how would you describe your energy levels and daily activities? Can you walk upstairs or do light chores?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m still active, lah. Walk 20 minutes most days, but I do get tired faster since the diabetes started. Still manage the garden and drive myself around.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. We’ll proceed with spinal anesthesia and local infiltration as planned. I’ll be with you throughout the surgery. Any questions before we begin?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] Spinal anesthesia administered with bupivacaine twelve point five milligrams.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:01] Oxygen via nasal cannula at two liters per minute initiated.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] Two large bore IVs placed, normal saline infusion at one hundred mL per hour.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] Blood pressure seventy over forty noted, administering one liter normal saline bolus.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:07] Heart rate forty, administering atropine one milligram IV.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Mr Tan, how are you feeling now after the TURP procedure?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I’m a bit uncomfortable, Doctor, but not in severe pain. More like a dull ache.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how would you rate your pain right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About 4, I’d say. It’s there, but the medication seems to be helping.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any nausea, dizziness, or breathing difficulties since waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, but I felt a bit light-headed when I first opened my eyes. Breathing’s fine though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything about the procedure itself while under spinal anesthesia?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I recall being awake and hearing voices, but it’s all hazy. Not much detail, really.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Given your hypertension, diabetes, and kidney condition, have you noticed any unusual symptoms like chest pain, blurred vision, or reduced urine output?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No chest pain or vision issues. Urine came out normally when I voided earlier. Blood sugar was 7.8 this morning, which is usual for me.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. We’ll continue monitoring your vitals, blood sugar, and kidney function. Any other concerns before we move you to the ward?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, Doctor. I’m just glad the procedure’s done. Thank you for checking on me.
